claims: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed test flight.
The Artemis II mission will follow a "figure-eight" trajectory.
The Artemis II mission will send four astronauts around the Moon and back.
The Artemis II mission will cover about 230,000 miles.
The Artemis II mission will launch from Kennedy Space Center.
The Artemis II mission will launch on the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Orion spacecraft will perform two high Earth orbits for system checks.
The Orion spacecraft will execute a translunar injection (TLI) burn to travel to the Moon.
The SLS rocket will lift off from Pad 39B.
The SLS rocket will insert Orion into a high elliptical orbit.
The high elliptical orbit involves a perigee raising maneuver.
The high elliptical orbit is for initial checkouts.
The crew will perform a manual handling exercise.
The crew will separate from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS).
Crew separation from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) is to test maneuvering capabilities.
Orion's main engine will fire for translunar injection (TLI).
Orion's main engine is via the European Service Module.
Firing of Orion's main engine puts the spacecraft on a trajectory toward the Moon.
The spacecraft will fly to the far side of the Moon.
The spacecraft will fly roughly 3,000 to 9,000 miles above the Moon's surface.
The spacecraft will use the Moon’s gravity to slingshot back toward Earth.
The spacecraft will not enter orbit around the Moon.
The return trip will take four days.
Re-entry speed will be over 25,000 mph.
Splashdown will be in the Pacific Ocean.
The Artemis II mission is designed to test the crew systems in deep space.
The Artemis II mission will take the crew farther from Earth than any previous human mission.
